messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a 15-25% tail latency bump on /v1/embeddings-rerank starting ~1923420000, coinciding with a traffic shift to bulk non-chat queries. Profiled a canary and saw weird kernel selection + KV cache churn. :eyes:
jordan: Ack, saw the alert. Any flamegraphs/pprof you'd share?
maria: Pushed two profiles to the artifact link: flamegraph + per-kernel time breakdown. Short summary: attention kernel chosen was generic fp32 path even though we run int8-quantized model for smaller sequences. Costly copies between kernels causing stalls. Also, queue snapshots show many tiny batches interleaved with huge 8k-token jobs — batching heuristic mixing lengths.
kai: That explains the thundering; if kernel selection falls back to non-quantized path you pay memcpy and extra transpose. Any nvprof traces?
maria: nvprof attached (see artifacts). Also noticed KV cache eviction spikes when we interleave long-batch and short-batch requests — working set oscillates. Looks like continuous-batcher early-fill logic is merging requests regardless of token budget skew.
ashley: Do we have a simple repro? Maybe run a synthetic mix: 70% short (128 tok), 30% long (4k tok) and observe batching behavior.
dmitri: I ran that locally. With current batcher config (max_batch_tokens=4096, early_fill_ms=5) the batcher often forms 4k-laden batches that force kernel -> slow path and evict KV for subsequent shorts. Throughput drops ~18%.
maria: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) kernel_affinity hint to prefer quantized kernel when all requests in batch are <= 512 tokens; 2) queue shaping to segregate by length buckets (<=512, 512-2048, >2048) and maintain separate continuous-batcher queues; 3) token_budget_target per queue to avoid mixing.
jordan: I like separate queues. Implementation-wise, we can add a lightweight histogram classifier in gateway that tags request.length_bucket and route to shard. Low risk and reversible.
kai: For kernel_affinity, runtime needs an API to accept hint from batcher: e.g., batch_meta.preferred_kernel = "int8_shortseq". Runtime will validate compatibility and select kernel. Minimal change.
nashley: Also think about KV warmup: before attaching long job to a queue, we can prefetch KV for the model shard if last_eviction_time < threshold. Might reduce cold misses.
dmitri: Did a micro-canary with separate queues + kernel hint in staging. Results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved 12%, p99 improved 22%, overall cost per token down ~6%. Will push the metrics snapshot to the doc.
maria: Nice. Any regression risk? Mixing queues might increase scheduling variance under low load.
jordan: True. We'll add a fallback that merges buckets if queue length < merge_threshold for X ms. Keep early-fill disabled when merging.
kai: Implementation plan: 1) gateway histogram classifier (fast, no external deps) 2) batcher support for batch_meta.preferred_kernel and token_budget_target string field 3) runtime kernel selection honor affinity unless incompatible 4) KV prefetch hook as optional flag.
maria: Timeline request: can we get a small canary to 10% internal traffic in 48h? dmitri, can you coordinate?
dmitri: Yes, will cut canary tomorrow morning. I'll add observability: per-queue latency, kernel_choice_count, kv_eviction_rate, merge_events.
perf-bot: Deploy plan checklist created: [ ] gateway change, [ ] batcher changes, [ ] runtime kernel affinity, [ ] KV prefetch flag, [ ] canary metrics dashboard. Link: https://internal.redwood/plots/1923456789-canary
jordan: Metrics to watch during canary: p99 latency, kernel_mismatch_errors, kv_eviction_rate, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu occupancy.
kai: Small note: ensure kernel selection has a graceful fallback policy that logs but continues. Don't throw errors on unknown affinity.
maria: Agreed. Also add quick A/B: canary A = separate queues only; canary B = queues + kernel affinity + kv prefetch. Compare cost+latency.
dmitri: I'll set that up. If A already gives most wins, we can delay kernel change.
maria: OK — sounds good. Thanks team. I'll add the action items to the RFC draft. :rocket:
